translations.answer: In H2O's H1 pipeline, a privileged motion imitator tracks every retargeted motion in closed loop and removes failed sequences. This exposes labels made infeasible by contact, inertia, or controller bandwidth more effectively than kinematic thresholds alone. It is a useful pre-training data gate, but passing it does not guarantee safety on another robot or on hardware.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Human motions are first retargeted to the target robot morphology.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: The feasibility policy uses controller and termination boundaries representative of the final tracking stack.
translations.applicability.robots.0: Unitree H1 in the H2O setup
translations.applicability.simulators.0: Isaac Gym / PhysX in the official implementation
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper includes controlled filtering and data-size ablations plus broad H1 demonstrations, and the pinned official repository exposes per-sequence closed-loop evaluation and failure-driven motion sampling. Confidence is capped because filtering thresholds and real-world robustness are tied to one robot/control stack and long-duration safety statistics are not reported.
